title: Do Not Be Anxious 不要忧虑 — Matthew 6:25–34

sections.heading: Do Not Be Anxious 不要忧虑
body: Matthew 6:25–34 马太福音 6:25–34
Friday Small Group · 2026-10-02

sections.heading: Scripture 经文 — Matthew 6:25–34 马太福音
sections.keyPhrase: "Do not be anxious about your life" 「不要为生命忧虑」 (v.25)

verses.cuv: 「所以我告诉你们，不要为生命忧虑吃甚么，喝甚么；为身体忧虑穿甚么。生命不胜于饮食么？身体不胜于衣裳么？
verses.web: Therefore I tell you, don’t be anxious for your life: what you will eat, or what you will drink; nor yet for your body, what you will wear. Isn’t life more than food, and the body more than clothing?

verses.cuv: 你们看那天上的飞鸟，也不种，也不收，也不积蓄在仓里，你们的天父尚且养活他。你们不比飞鸟贵重得多吗？
verses.web: See the birds of the sky, that they don’t sow, neither do they reap, nor gather into barns. Your heavenly Father feeds them. Aren’t you of much more value than they?

verses.cuv: 你们那一个能用思虑使寿数多加一刻呢〔或作：使身量多加一肘呢〕？
verses.web: “Which of you, by being anxious, can add one moment to his lifespan?

verses.cuv: 何必为衣裳忧虑呢？你想野地里的百合花怎么长起来；它也不劳苦，也不纺线。
verses.web: Why are you anxious about clothing? Consider the lilies of the field, how they grow. They don’t toil, neither do they spin,

verses.cuv: 然而我告诉你们，就是所罗门极荣华的时候，他所穿戴的，还不如这花一朵呢！
verses.web: yet I tell you that even Solomon in all his glory was not dressed like one of these.

verses.cuv: 你们这小信的人哪！野地里的草今天还在，明天就丢在炉里，神还给它这样的妆饰，何况你们呢！
verses.web: But if God so clothes the grass of the field, which today exists, and tomorrow is thrown into the oven, won’t he much more clothe you, you of little faith?

verses.cuv: 所以，不要忧虑说：吃甚么？喝甚么？穿甚么？
verses.web: “Therefore don’t be anxious, saying, ‘What will we eat?’, ‘What will we drink?’ or, ‘With what will we be clothed?’

verses.cuv: 这都是外邦人所求的，你们需用的这一切东西，你们的天父是知道的。
verses.web: For the Gentiles seek after all these things; for your heavenly Father knows that you need all these things.

verses.cuv: 你们要先求他的国和他的义，这些东西都要加给你们了。
verses.web: But seek first God’s Kingdom, and his righteousness; and all these things will be given to you as well.

verses.cuv: 所以，不要为明天忧虑，因为明天自有明天的忧虑；一天的难处一天当就彀了。」
verses.web: Therefore don’t be anxious for tomorrow, for tomorrow will be anxious for itself. Each day’s own evil is sufficient.

sections.heading: Context 背景
body: Part of the Sermon on the Mount 登山宝训.
The "therefore" in v.25 hangs on vv.19–24: treasures in heaven, "no one can serve two masters — God and money."
The anxiety Jesus addresses results from serving the wrong master.
His audience were subsistence farmers — food and clothing were real daily uncertainties.
This is trust taught to the insecure, not advice to the comfortable.

sections.heading: Original Language 原文
body: μεριμνάω (merimnaō) — to be pulled apart by care, divided in mind; same root as Martha "anxious and troubled" (Luke 10:41).
Present tense: "stop being anxious" — a habit to break.
Note merimnaō can be good — Paul uses it for Timothy's care for the church (Phil 2:20).
The issue is what divides you, not whether you care.

sections.heading: Cross-references 交叉经文
body: Luke 12:22–31 — parallel; "little flock, fear not"
Philippians 4:6–7 — the replacement: prayer with thanksgiving → peace
1 Peter 5:7 — "cast all your anxiety on him"
Psalm 55:22 — OT root
Matthew 6:19–24 — the cause, immediately before

sections.heading: Discussion 讨论
questions: Where does anxiety actually show up in your week? Name the top one or two.
Jesus ties anxiety to "serving two masters" (vv.24–25). Is there a treasure behind your top anxiety?
merimnaō means "pulled apart, divided." What is the difference, concretely, between responsible planning and being divided?
v.33 "seek first the kingdom" — if anxiety shrinks only when the central concern changes, what would "seeking first" look like in the situation you named in Q1?
Philippians 4:6–7 gives the replacement habit. What is one practice you could actually keep this week? Pick it from the Life menu and tell one person which you chose.

rows.practice: Fixed wind-down: phone away + Matt 6:34 + lights out at a set time, 5 nights.
Tell one trusted person your top anxiety; ask them to pray for it once.
One meal where each person names a time God provided when they worried.
Write the worry down, mark "today's or tomorrow's?" (v.34), park tomorrow's on paper.
Phil 4:6 reflex: one sentence of request + one of thanksgiving each time anxiety rises.
Review one recurring expense that exists to quiet anxiety; decide about it.
Pray v.33 daily: "what does seeking first look like today?" — one written line each morning.

sections.heading: Reflection 反思
body: Tuesday check-in: did the practice happen? What blocked it?
Thursday check-in: when anxiety rose, did the practice change what you did next?
End of week: what changed in you, in your own words?
Privacy rule: reflections are private by default; sharing is opt-in.
